title: 🔬 Thursday — Research: Energy Relationships Among Plants and Animals
note: Your Mission: Become a science researcher! Over the next two days, independently research one organism and learn how it gets and uses energy in its environment. Use your research to create a short presentation about your organism and its role in an ecosystem. You will work independently.
extra: Due Thursday, Oct 29 at 11:59 PM. Points: 10. Submitting: a text entry box or a file upload. Available Oct 29 at 8:20 AM through Nov 12 at 11:59 PM.
additionalSteps: What kind of environment does your organism live in?
What does your organism eat, or how does it get food?
Where does your organism get its energy?
What other organisms eat your organism?
Is your organism a producer, consumer, or scavenger? Explain your answer.
If your organism is a consumer, is it a herbivore, carnivore, or omnivore? Explain.
How does energy from the Sun eventually reach your organism?
What is one interesting fact you learned about your organism?

subject: Art
title: 🎨 Funny Imaginary Creature Art Project 🖼️📸
note: Grades 3–5: Build and paint a funny imaginary creature that could never exist in real life! Then upload a photo of your finished sculpture.
extra: Planned for Thursday, Oct 29. Teacher’s due date: Nov 6 at 11:59 PM. Points: 100. Submitting: a file upload. Available Oct 26 at 12:00 AM through Nov 13 at 11:59 PM.
instructionSteps: Gather safe materials you have at home: clay or air-dry clay; cardboard or paper rolls; clean recycled boxes or containers; paper, tape, or glue; paint and a brush, or markers and colored paper. Optional decorations: yarn or foil.
Imagine a creature that does not exist. Plan its shape and funny features.
Choose materials and build your creature as a sculpture.
Add details such as horns, wings, extra eyes, or a silly tail.
Let glue or air-dry clay dry as needed.
Paint your sculpture and let the paint dry.
instructionHeading: Take a photo, submit, and check your work
additionalSteps: Place your sculpture in a bright spot with a plain background if possible.
Take a clear photo showing the whole sculpture.
Upload the photo to the art assignment and submit it. If you need to label your work, use your first name only.
Before checking off this assignment: I built an imaginary creature sculpture; I added details and painted it; I took a clear photo of the whole sculpture; I uploaded and submitted my photo.

Parent/Caregiver Helper Note: Help find safe, available materials and use tools appropriately. An adult may help take or upload the photo, but let the student make the artwork and creative choices. Check that the photo clearly shows the artwork and does not include personal information.
